players.product: Custom data-center AI silicon (new entrant; hyperscaler custom-ASIC engagement)

quarterly_data.signal: 10-K supplier disclosure: other than certain RFFE modules and RF filter products, Qualcomm's QCT uses a fabless model and relies on third parties for the manufacturing, assembly and most of the testing of its integrated circuits, under turnkey and two-stage manufacturing models. Its primary foundry suppliers for digital, analog/mixed-signal, RF and PM integrated circuits include Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing Company (TSMC), Samsung Electronics and Global Foundries; its primary semiconductor assembly and test suppliers are Advanced Semiconductor Engineering, Amkor Technology, Siliconware Precision Industries and STATSChipPAC.

10-K: purchase obligations at September 28, 2025, primarily purchase commitments with certain suppliers of its integrated circuit products including those under multi-year capacity commitments, totaled $15.1 billion, of which $10.5 billion is expected to be paid in the next 12 months. Advance payments related to multi-year capacity purchase commitments were $1.9 billion at September 28, 2025 versus $3.0 billion at September 29, 2024.
quarterly_data.figure: purchase obligations $15.1 billion ($10.5 billion in next 12 months); capacity-commitment advance payments $1.9 billion (September 28, 2025) vs $3.0 billion (September 29, 2024)

quarterly_data.signal: 10-K: cash outflows for capital expenditures were $1.2 billion in fiscal 2025 and $1.0 billion in fiscal 2024; Qualcomm expects capital expenditures to increase from fiscal 2025 in the near term primarily to support the testing of its integrated circuits.
